THOUGHT: The patient has a month-long continuous headache with recent dizziness and nausea that markedly improve when he goes outside into cold air — a pattern suggestive of an environmental inhalational exposure (symptoms improve with fresh air/ventilation). He’s been living in a cabin for 5 weeks, a setting with potential for chronic low-level carbon monoxide (CO) exposure from heating/combustion without good ventilation.

The CBC shows marked erythrocytosis (Hgb 20 g/dL, Hct 60%), which can be secondary to chronic tissue hypoxia driving increased EPO. Chronic CO exposure produces impaired oxygen delivery (carboxyhemoglobin) and can lead to compensatory secondary polycythemia over weeks. A normal pulse oximetry reading (98%) is unreliable in CO exposure because pulse oximeters cannot distinguish oxyhemoglobin from carboxyhemoglobin and often read spuriously normal/high. 

Primary polycythemia vera could also present with elevated Hgb/Hct and neurologic symptoms, but PV more often has constitutional signs (pruritus after hot shower, splenomegaly), possible leukocytosis/thrombocytosis, and would not explain the clear improvement of symptoms outdoors after fresh air. The temporal association with staying in a poorly ventilated cabin and symptomatic relief outside, together with high Hgb/Hct and a normal pulse oximeter, strongly favors chronic CO exposure causing secondary erythrocytosis.

DIAGNOSIS: Chronic carbon monoxide exposure causing secondary polycythemia (secondary erythrocytosis).
